alignments.note: Rule 30: the waw and the emphatic ʾap are rendered by the single word *Yea*, which carries both; headed on ʾap under rule 23 as the morpheme carrying the content. Competing reading: *Yea* to the waw alone under rule 14 with ʾap unrepresented.
Rule 17: subject pronoun and auxiliaries join the verb, headed on *allured*.

Rule 30: preposition plus construct noun rendered by the one compound preposition *out of* (margin: *Hebrew out of the mouth of*); headed on the construct noun, target head on the lexeme-bearing *out* under rule 24.
Rule 33/15: the supplied *Into a* belongs to this nominal, whose terminative case-function licenses it; rule 31 heads on *broad*, since *place* alone is any place.
Rule 22/30: the preposition with its resumptive suffix is written as the single pronominal adverb *where*, headed on the preposition since no relative morpheme stands here.
Rule 20: the presentative frame *there is* joins the unit bearing the predicate, headed on *straitness*; discontinuous around *no* under rule 25.
Rule 46: the construct noun is recast as *that which is set*, the supplied noun phrase and verb naming the noun's own lexeme; headed on *set*.
Rule 19: the construct relation recast with *on* belongs to the nomen rectum, headed on *table*; discontinuous around *thy* under rule 25.

Corrected. Rule 44: `דֶשֶׁן` is a bare accusative of material — no preposition and no object marker on it — and the English predicate reaches that complement only through the supplied *of*, so the word belongs to `מָלֵא`'s unit, exactly as `תְּבַצְּעִי רֵעַיִךְ` → *hast greedily gained of thy neighbors* gives its *of* to the verb; the auxiliary and copula join it under rules 17 and 20, headed on *full*. This is the reading JOB.36.17 takes for the same construction. Competing reading: rule 33's supplied preposition on an adverbial accusative, which the accepted alignment took; rejected because *full* admits no other word before its complement, so the *of* states the predicate's valency rather than what the noun contributes.
Noun takes *fatness*; the *of* standing before it is `מָלֵא`'s under rule 44 and not this noun's under rule 33.

review_notes: Corrected for cross-verse consistency with JOB.36.17: the supplied *of* after *full* is the predicate's under rule 44, not the noun's under rule 33. Word order is not what decides it — Hebrew writes such a complement before its predicate at 36.17 and after it here.
Only the s017/s018 boundary moved; every other unit is retained verbatim from the accepted alignment, including the rule 30 fusions at *Yea* and *out of* and the rule 22 fusion at *where*.
The marginal *Hebrew out of the mouth of* was read and set aside under rule 38; it corroborates the *out of* fusion without deciding it, by rule 7.
*where* is placed on taḥteyhā under rule 22 rather than marked a supplied subordinator under rule 55, since a preposition and a resumptive suffix stand there for it.
All eighteen source ids and all thirty-one target ids are partitioned exactly once.
